config.description: Application configuration, using the same YAML schema as config.yaml. Secrets are references such as { env: ADMIN_PASSWORD }, supplied through env or envFrom. Omitted settings use application defaults. Rendered through tpl with the release context. Mutually exclusive with existingConfigMap.
config.title: config

database.description:
Three Postgres connection strings, each from its own Secret. The
application role must not own the tables (row-level security), the owner
role runs migrations and applies configuration on the leader, and the
runner role is handed to runner Jobs and can only write its own run. On
CloudNativePG, declare `app` and `runner` as DatabaseRole resources and
use the bootstrap owner as `owner`; see the database docs.

existingSecret.description: (required) Secret holding the application role's connection URI.
existingSecret.title: existingSecret

role.description: Name of the application role, asserted at startup (not superuser, no BYPASSRLS, owns nothing).
role.title: role

existingSecret.description: (required) Secret holding the owner role's connection URI, used only by the leader for migrations and configuration sync.
existingSecret.title: existingSecret

existingSecret.description: (required) Secret holding the runner role's connection URI; referenced by runner Jobs, never read by kritika serve.
existingSecret.title: existingSecret

role.description: Name of the runner role, granted only what runner Jobs need.
role.title: role

database.title: database

deploymentAnnotations.description: Annotations added to the Deployment (e.g. `reloader.stakater.com/auto: "true"`). Pod-level annotations go in `podAnnotations`.
deploymentAnnotations.title: deploymentAnnotations

env.description: Operational settings and referenced secrets, keyed by environment variable name. Use valueFrom.secretKeyRef for credentials. Do not duplicate file settings or chart-managed variables. Rendered through tpl.
env.title: env

envFrom.description: Secrets and ConfigMaps loaded as environment variables in bulk. Keys must match the secret references in config. Application settings must not also be set in the file.
envFrom.title: envFrom

existingConfigMap.description: Existing ConfigMap containing config.yaml instead of inline config. Put webUrl in that file. Changes require a restart, for example through a Reloader annotation.
existingConfigMap.title: existingConfigMap

gatewayCache.description:
The gateway's download cache: each kritika serve replica keeps what a
repository's locked tools download, and what runner tools download from the
hosts `config.egress.cache` names, in an emptyDir, and serves it again to
the next run that asks for the same URL, so a tool is fetched once per
replica rather than once per run. mise still checks every download against
the repository's lock.

enabled.description: Give each replica an emptyDir for the cache (KRITIKA_GATEWAY_CACHE_DIR), which keeps what a repository's `.kritika/mise.lock` pins; `config.egress.cache` names more hosts whose downloads it keeps.
enabled.title: enabled

maxAge.description: How long a kept download is served before it is fetched again (KRITIKA_GATEWAY_CACHE_MAX_AGE), a Go duration.
maxAge.title: maxAge

maxSize.description: The most the cache keeps (KRITIKA_GATEWAY_CACHE_MAX_SIZE), in bytes or with Ki, Mi, Gi or Ti, the least recently used downloads going first, and apart from that the most its fetches under way may write. Allow ephemeral storage for twice this size plus evicted files still being served and the pod's other storage use. Evicted files retain disk space until their readers finish, for up to two minutes; their total size is not bounded by this setting.
maxSize.title: maxSize

gatewayCache.title: gatewayCache

image.description:
Default values for kritika.

Most string, list and map values below are rendered through Helm's `tpl`, so
they may carry template expressions that resolve at install time, e.g.
  ingress.hosts[0].host: kritika.{{ .Values.global.domain }}
Plain numbers and booleans are passed through as they are.

digest.description: Pin the image by digest (sha256:…); when set, overrides the tag. The release pipeline fills it with the published image's digest.
digest.title: digest

tag.description: Overrides the image tag; defaults to the chart appVersion.
tag.title: tag

image.title: image

imagePullSecrets.description: Image pull secrets for private registries, for the kritika serve pods and, through the runner ServiceAccount, runner Jobs.
imagePullSecrets.title: imagePullSecrets

ingress.description:
One Ingress, or one Gateway API HTTPRoute, to the public Service, which
serves the webhooks under `/hooks` and the dashboard. Its host must be
`config.webUrl`'s: GitHub delivers webhooks to that URL and sign-in
redirects back to it, so a route for another name serves a dashboard
that cannot sign in.

enabled.title: enabled

hosts.description: Ingress hosts and their paths; the host is `config.webUrl`'s.
hosts.title: hosts

allowCrossNamespaceImport.title: allowCrossNamespaceImport

matchLabels.title: matchLabels

additionalRuleAnnotations.title: additionalRuleAnnotations

additionalRuleLabels.description: Extra labels on every alert rule, e.g. a routing label for Alertmanager. The rule's own `severity` wins.
additionalRuleLabels.title: additionalRuleLabels

configDriftFor.description: How long a replica's configuration file may differ from the applied one before KritikaConfigDrift fires; a rollout drifts briefly until the new leader applies its file.
configDriftFor.title: configDriftFor

configErrorFor.description: How long the leader's latest apply of the configuration may stay refused before KritikaConfigError fires.
configErrorFor.title: configErrorFor

multipleLeadersFor.description: How long more than one replica may report the lock before KritikaMultipleLeaders fires. A database failover can show two for one leader retry interval.
multipleLeadersFor.title: multipleLeadersFor

queueAgeSeconds.description: Oldest runnable review/followup/thread job age in seconds that triggers KritikaQueueDelayed. Index onboarding is excluded; its age remains on the dashboard.
queueAgeSeconds.title: queueAgeSeconds

queueDelayFor.description: How long runnable work must exceed queueAgeSeconds before warning.
queueDelayFor.title: queueDelayFor

queueStatsUnavailableFor.description: How long every scraped replica may succeed on fewer than 75% of queue snapshot reads over 5 minutes before warning.
queueStatsUnavailableFor.title: queueStatsUnavailableFor

vectorSearchErrorsFor.description: How long the vector-search error ratio must exceed 10% (at least 10 non-canceled requests in 15 minutes) before warning.
vectorSearchErrorsFor.title: vectorSearchErrorsFor

networkPolicy.description:
NetworkPolicies (off by default): one for the service pods (ingress to the
webhook and metrics ports, and to the gateway port from runner pods;
egress to the cluster's DNS, the forges and models over the egress ports,
Postgres and the API server) and one for runner pods (egress only: the
cluster's DNS, Postgres and the gateway port on the service pods, through
which everything else is reached). Runner pods reach the Postgres port
only where `postgres` says the database is; the service pods reach it at
any address, as they do the egress ports.

allowDNS.description: Allow DNS egress (UDP/TCP 53) to the cluster's DNS, as `dns` describes it, and nowhere else.
allowDNS.title: allowDNS

dns.description: The cluster's DNS, the one peer the pods may send port 53 to.

namespace.description: Namespace of the cluster's DNS pods.
namespace.title: namespace

nodeLocalAddresses.description: Addresses of a NodeLocal DNSCache on each node's own network, such as `169.254.20.10`, which the pods query in place of those pods. The Cilium flavor allows DNS to the node itself instead, since Cilium gives the node's addresses the host's identity.
nodeLocalAddresses.title: nodeLocalAddresses

podSelector.description:
Empty rather than kube-dns's label: Helm merges maps, so a default here
would stay beside the labels set in its place.
Labels of the cluster's DNS pods; empty stands for `k8s-app: kube-dns`.
podSelector.title: podSelector

runnerNames.description: With the Cilium flavor, the names runner pods may look up besides those of the cluster's Services, `<service>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local`, which the cluster's DNS answers itself (an ExternalName Service's goes on to the name its author set): the database's host when it is outside the cluster. Each is a name, or a Cilium `matchPattern` in which `*` stands for part of one label. Cilium refuses any other name; the other flavors do not filter names.
runnerNames.title: runnerNames

dns.title: dns

egressPorts.description: TCP ports the service pods may egress to for forges and model endpoints. Runner pods reach the gateway alone.
egressPorts.title: egressPorts

postgres.description:
Where the database the runner role's URI names is, the one peer runner
pods may reach postgresPort at: every pod in the release namespace unless
set.

cidrs.description: CIDRs of a database outside the cluster, such as `192.0.2.10/32`.
cidrs.title: cidrs

namespace.description: Namespace of the database's pods; the release namespace when empty.
namespace.title: namespace

podSelector.description: Labels of the database's pods, such as `cnpg.io/cluster: kritika-postgres` for a CloudNativePG cluster, or of the pods of a session-mode pooler the runner's URI goes through. Empty selects every pod in `namespace`, or none when only `cidrs` is set.
podSelector.title: podSelector

type.title: type

enabled.title: enabled

maxUnavailable.description: Maximum pods that may be unavailable, as a count or percentage; takes precedence over `minAvailable` when set.
maxUnavailable.title: maxUnavailable

minAvailable.description: Minimum pods that must stay available, as a count or percentage. Used unless `maxUnavailable` is set.
minAvailable.title: minAvailable

priorityClassName.description: PriorityClass for the pods. Empty uses the cluster default.
priorityClassName.title: priorityClassName

create.description: Create the Role and RoleBinding kritika serve needs: Jobs in the release namespace, their pods and logs, and the Secrets it hands them. Nothing cluster-wide.
create.title: create

readinessProbe.description: Readiness probe, on the metrics port. A replica is ready once its configuration file has loaded, the database answers and it serves webhooks and the dashboard, so a rollout takes the previous pod down only once the new one can hold a delivery.
readinessProbe.title: readinessProbe

replicas.description:
kritika runs as one Deployment of `kritika serve`: webhooks, the dashboard,
the job queues, runner Jobs, the gateway and, on the replica holding the
leader lock, the leader duties. Runner pods are not part of it: serve
creates them as Jobs, one per review, follow-up and index run.
Replicas of kritika serve. Every replica serves webhooks and the dashboard and works jobs; exactly one holds the leader lock at a time. A rollout keeps one serving on its own; set 2 for one to keep serving while a pod or node is lost.
replicas.title: replicas

resources.description: Resource requests and limits of the kritika serve pods.
resources.title: resources

runner.description:
Runner Jobs: one pod per review, follow-up or index run, created by kritika
serve in the release namespace from the release's -tools image, running as a
service account with no permissions and a database role that can only touch
its own run. The server's Role reaches every Secret in the release namespace,
so install kritika into a namespace of its own. A sandboxed RuntimeClass
(gVisor, Kata), `runner.podTemplate.spec.runtimeClassName`, is advised,
since a runner parses untrusted repository content and runs what the model
asks.

enabled.description: Have the cluster refuse, from kritika serve's ServiceAccount, any Job that is not a runner Job as kritika builds it, any Secret that is not a run's, and any deletion of a Job but in the foreground, which takes its run's Secret with it, with three ValidatingAdmissionPolicies and their bindings: cluster-scoped objects the chart's installer must be allowed to create. Without them the Role lets kritika serve create any Job in its namespace, whose pod may run as another ServiceAccount and mount another Secret. Any tag or digest of the runner image's repository passes, so the runs an older replica starts mid-rollout do too; changing the repository, the runner ServiceAccount, RuntimeClass, database Secret or a Secret the runner container's `env` names refuses them until the rollout ends, and they are retried.
enabled.title: enabled

jobTemplate.description:
What kritika sets on every runner Job (KRITIKA_RUNNER_JOB_TEMPLATE), as
a Job template spells it. The Job's retries, its pod failure policy and
its pod stay kritika's.

annotations.description: Annotations for runner Jobs. kritika refuses its own, under `kritika.home-operations.com/`.
annotations.title: annotations

labels.description: Labels for runner Jobs. kritika refuses its own, the instance label and the Job controller's.
labels.title: labels

activeDeadlineSeconds.description: How long a runner Job may run, in seconds: at most 7200, or River's job timeout cap would cut the run off early. A review's or follow-up's Job runs as long as its agent's `timeout`, for each part a review is split into, needs, if that is longer. The deadline bounds the work around the run and the run's gateway token too.
activeDeadlineSeconds.title: activeDeadlineSeconds

ttlSecondsAfterFinished.description: How long a finished Job stays for kubectl before Kubernetes removes it, in seconds; the run row keeps everything the Job knew.
ttlSecondsAfterFinished.title: ttlSecondsAfterFinished

jobTemplate.title: jobTemplate

podTemplate.description:
What kritika sets on every runner pod (KRITIKA_RUNNER_POD_TEMPLATE), as
a pod template spells it. What keeps a runner isolated, its
ServiceAccount, the token it does not mount, its security contexts, its
volumes and its command, stays kritika's.

annotations.description: Annotations for runner pods, such as `karpenter.sh/do-not-disrupt: "true"`. kritika refuses AppArmor's, which would set the runner's profile.
annotations.title: annotations

labels.description: Labels for runner pods. kritika refuses its own, the instance label and the Job controller's.
labels.title: labels

containers.description: The runner container, the pod's one, named runner: its `image`, empty for this release's `-tools` image pinned by digest, which adds mise with curl, fd, gh, jq, rg and yq for a review's or follow-up's run tool; its `imagePullPolicy`; and its `env`, variables the run tool's commands get over a repository's `[env]`, each a `value` or a Secret's key (`valueFrom.secretKeyRef`), which is masked out of what the commands print. kritika sets them on the container as `KRITIKA_COMMAND_ENV_<name>`, so they configure the commands and never kritika itself, and refuses the names it keeps for the commands, such as `HOME`, `PATH`, the proxy variables and `GH_*`. The Secret must be in the release namespace.
containers.title: containers

hostUsers.description: Set false to run runner pods in a user namespace of their own, which the nodes' kernel and container runtime must support; true shares the node's, as Kubernetes does by default.
hostUsers.title: hostUsers

nodeSelector.description: Node labels runner pods are scheduled by.
nodeSelector.title: nodeSelector

priorityClassName.description: PriorityClass for runner pods. Empty uses the cluster default.
priorityClassName.title: priorityClassName

resources.description: Requests and limits of cpu, memory and hugepages for the whole runner pod, the run tool's commands included: pod-level resources, on by default from Kubernetes 1.34. A LimitRange's container defaults in the release namespace still apply to the runner container: its default limit bounds the runner within the pod's, and the API refuses a runner pod whose requests are below its default requests.
resources.title: resources

runtimeClassName.description: RuntimeClass for runner pods, such as gvisor or kata. Empty uses the cluster default.
runtimeClassName.title: runtimeClassName

topologySpreadConstraints.description: Topology spread constraints for runner pods.
topologySpreadConstraints.title: topologySpreadConstraints

securityContext.title: securityContext

gatewayPort.title: gatewayPort

port.description: Public port: the webhooks (`POST /hooks/{app}`) and the dashboard.
port.title: port

type.description: Service type of the public Service.
type.title: type

automount.description: Automount the API token, which kritika serve needs to create runner Jobs.
automount.title: automount

create.description: Create the ServiceAccount kritika serve runs as.
create.title: create

name.description: ServiceAccount name; generated from the release name if empty.
name.title: name

startupProbe.description: Startup probe, on the metrics port. The liveness and readiness probes wait until it passes, so a pod still opening its listeners is not reported unready; it allows a minute.
startupProbe.title: startupProbe

strategy.description: Deployment update strategy. A rolling update that surges one pod and takes none down keeps a replica serving while each is replaced. Helm merges maps, so a switch to `Recreate` also sets `rollingUpdate: null`.
strategy.title: strategy

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Grace period for a clean shutdown: kritika serve keeps accepting webhooks, dashboard requests and model steps for 5s while traffic moves off the pod, stops taking jobs and lets running ones finish for up to 100s, then takes up to 90s to hand back the reviews it cut for a retry, and its gateway lets model steps in flight finish for up to 2m.
terminationGracePeriodSeconds.title: terminationGracePeriodSeconds

tests.description:
Config for the chart's `helm test` hook: a one-shot pod that curls the
metrics Service's /readyz to prove the release serves. Used only by `helm
test`, never the workload.

repository.title: repository

tests.title: tests

topologySpreadConstraints.title: topologySpreadConstraints
